title: The Spiritual Man as Microcosm of the Twelve Aeons: Five Faculties + Calling and Hearing
arc: The teaching glorifies the Twelve Great Aeons of Light and then shows that their structure is reproduced within the regenerate man as members: the five faculties of the First Man together with the Calling and the Hearing make up the seven, in whom the Living Spirit dwells, the Ambassador stands firm, and the soul becomes a king in the likeness of the First Father.
reading:
The chapter opens as a doxology addressed to the Twelve Great Aeons of the Light — the complete articulation of heavenly states from the Father — and then asks the corresponding question: what are these Twelve Great Aeons of the Light, and how do they stand within the spiritual man? The whole teaching is the answer. It shows that the same structure which articulates the heavens articulates the regenerate human, so that the spiritual man holds the spiritual senses as members within him exactly as the Aeons stand within the Father's fullness.

The first move is to identify the foundation. "The lower one stands at the foremost" of the elements that dwell with the First Man: the lowest of the heavenly degrees is the very element that takes its station first in the regenerate, because regeneration begins where the natural meets the spiritual. To this First Man as receptacle the Calling and the Hearing are joined and made manifest within. The teaching then gives its central arithmetic: "they become seven — the five with the two." The five are the discrete faculties of reception (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) — the Five Sons of the First Man understood interiorly as the five members of the spiritual organism. The two are the Call (Divine Truth's summons descending) and the Hearing (the soul's response ascending). Five inward faculties plus two motions of conjunction make seven: fullness in ultimates, the holy sabbath-completion of the inner man. This is what is meant by "the spiritual senses as members": the faculties are not external organs but interior members of one body, made complete only when the Call has come down and the Hearing has gone up through them.

The Living Spirit is then named as the one who dwells in these members and orders the whole cosmos through them; "likewise the Spirit … of the Man — they are one." The same operative Divine power that builds structure throughout the cosmos is the very spirit at work within the regenerate man, so that the order of the seven within him is not different from the order of the All. This is why the foremost blessing is named as "the cosmos established firm in him" — the entire cosmic order stands established in the spiritual man because he carries the same articulation in his members.

The latter half of the teaching shows how this inner order was made possible. There was a struggle in which what had been hidden was released into a region not yet manifest, lifted up against the Enemy; a hidden chamber was prepared; and the Ambassador, who came forth from the Father, came and stood firm in the midst of these things. He is called "the beautiful Father of all the Aeons," because in his standing-firm at the center the entire twelve-fold structure is held together and reproduced. Through him the holy ones who are joined become leaders and great kings in the likeness of the First Father, the Lord of all counsels — they who, in this very purpose of heart, fashion this cosmos unto the end of all its works.

The whole arc is therefore a teaching about correspondence in the strictest sense. The Twelve Aeons above, the seven (five-plus-two) members within the First Man, the one Living Spirit operative in both, the Ambassador standing firm at the center, and the regenerate as kings made in the likeness of the First Father — these are not parallel realities but one reality at different registers. The spiritual man holds the spiritual senses as members within him because he is built in the same form as the heavens: faculties opened by the Call, gathered by the Hearing, indwelt by the Spirit, centered on the Ambassador, and crowned in the likeness of the Father whose Aeons they reproduce.
